units.author: sb_bins
units.text: Thank you, Pell. I have now read the newsletter, as instructed. It says the round moves to Thursdays 'from Monday'. Which Monday? There are a great many Mondays, and the council has not specified one. In the meantime my boxes are in the hall, where my wife has named them. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: The Courier has it this morning: the hired lorry can't make the turn at the chapel end of Rope Walk, a replacement is promised 'within weeks', and a smaller van will do Thursdays until then. They also quote a retired postman who keeps a written log of his calls. I wonder who that could be.

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: A lorry too wide for the street it was hired to collect from. In forty-one years of driving buses I was never once given a vehicle that did not fit the route. The depot measured things. That was the whole point of the depot.

units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Fair enough Garvey, the grey box it is. This morning 06:05: working perfectly, green in under a minute both ways. I don't trust it. It's lulling us. Frost on the reservoir bridge, by the way, took the bend at walking pace and still felt the back step out.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Bus on time this morning for the first time in a week. My middle one says the driver did a little cheer at the junction. I'd like to think that's true. Also Sound FM says a lorry dropped straw on the Tollinby road this afternoon so I'm going the long way to pick up from rehearsal.

units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Evening run: straw everywhere past the mill, a farmer forking it back onto a trailer with the expression of a man who's been forking straw since before you were born. Lights at Brackwater stuck on red at 18:15 for six minutes. There it is. I knew it.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Lisle 07:15 left at 07:15. The coffee machine produced something brown and hot and I am choosing not to ask further questions. The power went off in Lisle west at about ten past eight, which I know because my neighbour texted me a photo of her toaster looking disappointed.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Brown and hot is the design specification. Anything beyond that is a bonus. On an unrelated note, if anyone has a spare fuel filter for a marine genset of a certain age lying about in their shed, I'm buying. The office has one 'on order', which in our office is a philosophical position, not a fact.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: The power cut in Lisle west closed the school kitchen for the morning, I'm told by the dinner lady, who used to be my dinner lady. The children had sandwiches and thought it a great adventure. Ewan, a toaster cannot look disappointed. It may look unplugged.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: I've read the decision notice so nobody else has to. ADC/VEG/0917, six conditions: 1. fuel and oil stored in bunded tanks; 2. no felling into the water, floating debris to be recovered; 3. nesting bird check (out of season, discharged); 4. burning only in a single approved pit, attended during working hours; 5. the landing to be reinstated after the works; 6. the council notified on completion. That's it. There is no application for any future use, because nobody has made one.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Gil, what would we expect to see if Ardent Vale were an ordinary private investor? A registered office at a law firm, no public staff list, a short statement saying nothing. Which is what we see. That doesn't prove they are ordinary, but it means the registered address isn't evidence of anything. The planning conditions, as quoted above, are the sort you'd attach to any big clearance.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: Bram, your father would have been in my husband's year at the Lisle school, if I have the right family. I remember the children drawing the Holm from the ferry window as a great green hump, every one of them. It will be strange to see the shape of the land underneath. I hope the people working there are being looked after properly; it's a long way out in the winter.

units.author: propwatch_ledger
units.text: Finding 1, for what it's worth: the Holm sale went through an intermediary company, not Ardent Vale directly, which matches what the Courier said. Finding 2: I haven't got the intermediary's name yet. The land registry search costs money and takes a few days, and I'm a retired bookkeeper, not a bank. I'll post when it comes back. Please don't run off with this, Gil.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: I have looked at those trees from my front window every day for eighty years, give or take the years I was in service in Weyhaven. I shall miss the shape of them, I think, though I can't say I ever wished to go across. My mother always said the Holm was the best view in the Sound and nobody's business beyond that. I thinkk she was right on both counts.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Ferrous, with respect, 'ordinary private investors' don't buy islands through middlemen and then strip them bare in a month. Why the hurry? Why thirty days? You can't build anything on an island in winter. So what's the clearance FOR? Nobody can answer that, and the people who could are being paid not to. I've started a mailing list for anyone who wants updates.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: Gil, clearing in winter and building in spring is the normal sequence, not a mystery. You fell outside the bird nesting season because condition 3 makes you, and you don't want the site lying open for a year. As for 'what it's for': owners aren't obliged to say until they apply for something. When they do, it'll be on the portal, and I'll read that too.

units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Ha, thanks Bram, I'll keep the nets in mind for when the van finally dies. Rang Grieve's office this afternoon. Nice woman, very polite, said the Holm crew is 'fully resourced' and took my number. Fully resourced is office for no. I'll stick an ad in Trades and Jobs anyway, somebody always needs a saw.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Aye, Mrs Hale, that's the right family. Father talked about the Lisle school till the day he died, mostly about the cane. The hump's a fair description. Went past the landing on the morning tide and they've a clearing cut already, bigger than yesterday. You can hear the axes across the water when it's still. Carries a long way, does a sound like that.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Gil, please don't advertise your mailing list in this thread; there's a board for announcements. And a gentle general note: the people working on the Holm are doing a job, and it's their job, not a conspiracy. Questions about the owner's plans are fair game. Questions about the crew are not.

units.author: gilliver_teen
units.text: bram you can hear axes from the harbour? i've been on the wall all evening and all i can hear is gulls and my mate's car stereo. maybe you've got special fisherman ears. or maybe it's the chippy extractor fan, that thing sounds like someone chopping wood if you're desperate enough

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Planning lady explains it in four sentences. Gil writes a paragraph about 'what it's FOR'. It's for money, Gil. Everything's for money. That's not a conspiracy, that's a Tuesday. Now somebody tell me why the Tollinby road was covered in straw.

units.title: Missing: Pebble, small grey cat, Tanners Lane, Port Ammet
units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: Pebble has been missing since this morning. She's small, grey, with one white sock on her front left paw and a notch in her right ear from an argument with a gull. She went out of the back door at seven and didn't come in for breakfast, which she has never missed in four years. Sound FM kindly read it out at ten past six. Please check your sheds and garages, she's shy and might hide if she's frightened. Thank you so much.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Moved to Lost and Found and pinned for a week. I've had a look in our garage on Coopers Yard, which backs onto Tanners Lane, and there's no cat, only the ghost of the bicycle I keep meaning to mend. I'll look again in the morning. Best of luck.

units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: I park the van in the lock-up on Tanners Lane, number 6. Had the doors open this afternoon to sort my kit, so she might have nipped in. I'll check behind the chain oil drums first thing. If she's in there she'll smell of two-stroke, sorry in advance.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Not local to you, but one thing that worked for our old cat: shake the biscuit box at the back door last thing at night when it's quiet. They hear it further than you'd think. And leave something that smells of you on the step. Ours turned up two days later in next door's greenhouse looking furious.

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: We read Pebble out again on the overnight show at half one, between a man ringing about his allotment and a woman who just wanted to say she'd finished her shift. The presenter did the white sock detail twice because he liked it. Fingers crossed.

units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: Thank you Pell, thank you Davey (two-stroke is fine, I'd take her smelling of anything), thank you TollinbyMum, I'm doing the biscuit box now. I've put her blanket on the back step. The street's very quiet. Mrs Ober's two cats next door are both indoors, which they never are, so at least they're not fighting.

units.title: gilliver chippy hours (official)
units.author: gilliver_teen
units.text: public service announcement from the chippy since the owner doesnt do the internet: closed mondays from now on, open till 21:30 the rest of the week, last orders 21:15. its because of the price of fryer oil and NOT because of me, whatever my brother says. curry sauce is back

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Thank you, Kit. Tell your boss the haddock on Thursday was the best in the Sound and the chips were a disgrace. He'll know what I mean. He's known what I mean for thirty year.

units.title: Carrow Point weather station: daily summaries.
units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Starting a fresh thread for the daily numbers, as the old one got long enough to need its own postcode. Yesterday at the Point: max 9.4°C, min 2.1°C, pressure 1024 hPa steady, wind NW 9 knots dropping to 3 by midnight. Rain nil. Dew point 1.8°C at 06:00 today, which with a light wind means mist in the hollows. The Met Office says fog later in the week. I agree with them, for once.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Welcome back to the daily numbers. If the fog comes as advection fog off the sea rather than radiation fog in the valleys, it'll sit on the Sound for days at this time of year. Anyone crossing at night should allow for the ferry slowing right down. I measured visibility of under fifty metres at the Lisle slip in a week like that once.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Exactly right, Ferrous. Evening reading: 1025 hPa, wind calm, temperature 4.0°C and falling 0.8 an hour, dew point 2.9°C. The gap is closing. Not tonight, I think, but the sea temperature is still 11°C, and once a light southerly gets going over that, we'll have textbook advection fog. I'm unreasonably excited.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: The chart has Carrow Point as four flashes every twenty seconds. A dropped flash isn't a hazard to anyone with a chart and a watch, but it's quite right to report it, Maud. The light's whole job is to be exactly the same every night, so you notice when it isn't.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: Thank you both. It was giving its four again when I looked at half past eleven, so you were quite right about midnight. I shan't ring anybody. It is a comfort to know a thing like a battery can be cold. I had always thought of the light as more or less a person.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Confirmed from the notice on the hall doors: north aisle first, then east, then the fish counter end. East aisle closes in three weeks' time. So eucalyptus and cat bed have a little while yet, though I've seen the cat news since and I'm very sorry.

units.title: Kingfisher and the King: tickets, costumes, sanity.
units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: The Courier has done a piece on the Tollinby primary play, so here's the practical bit. Tickets free from the school office or the bookshop. Costume sessions are Wednesday evenings in the church hall. They need blue fabric, badly. My middle one is a Bulrush and has been practising standing very still and swaying, which is more than she does for homework.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: The tickets are behind my counter, between the poetry and the local history, as promised. Forty gone today. One small boy came in with his grandmother and asked whether reeds have lines. I said I believed the Second Reed did. He said 'that's me' and walked out an inch taller.

units.title: Lisle ferry passes kept. Good.
units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: I see the Courier quotes 'a former teacher at Lisle's primary school'. I said rather more than that, and rather better, but the gist survived. The passes matter. A child who has to choose between the college and a day's wages on a boat will often choose the boat, and you can't always blame them.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: I had one of those passes, Mrs Hale, on the old boat, before the upper lounge had seats. It is the only reason I have an office job to complain about now. Also, the Courier 'has not independently verified' the coffee machine. I can verify it. It exists.

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: Morning Irena love, I come in at five every day off the depot and walk up to 5 in the dark half the time because the button on 4 is broken too and I've never heard a thing on those stairs, not a squeak, which if anything I find more worrying because you'd expect somebody, wouldn't you, in a building this size, mind how you go and knock on mine if you want company down

units.author: dc_7_irena
units.text: Dear Hassan, thank you, the bread arrived at a quarter to seven and was still warm, and I did not need the stairs at all. Dear Lorna, thank you, I may take you up on it. Dear Jordie, I have put the list under your door. Please note that 'the good biscuits' means the oat ones. Irena, 7C

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Measured the stair timers tonight, in case it's useful for the Kerrow complaint. 1. One press on 6, 7 or 8 gives 45 seconds (n=5). 2. The button on 7 gives 22 seconds unless held, as Hassan says. 3. Climbing 6 to 8 at a normal pace takes me 50 seconds. 4. So the lights will go out on everyone between 6 and 8, every time, by design. That part at least is simple.

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: tobin out here with a stopwatch at 9pm. respect honestly. so the stairs are literally designed to plunge you into darkness halfway up. the cardio of doom is a feature not a bug. got Irena's list btw, oat biscuits secured, i also got her the fancy jam by accident and she can have it

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Tobin, thank you, I've pasted that straight into the email to Kerrow. Numbered and everything. If it gets a reply I'll frame it. Residents' meeting soon to talk about the lift and the lights together, date to follow once I can get the community room. Bev, DCRA

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Sheet is filling up nicely, thank you all. Benedikt evenings, Tobin Saturdays, Jordie weekends, Hassan's nephew after school. Kerrow say the part is now 'in transit'. I asked from where. They said 'from the supplier'. So that's that cleared up. Bev

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: Took up shopping for 13B and 14A tonight. 14A gave me a slice of cake, which was not necessary but was good. Lights on the stairs went out twice on the way up, between 7 and 8 both times, as Tobin says. I just stand and wait and press again. It is fine.

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: My nephew did four flats today and asked for a raise. I said the raise is the stairs, they will make him strong. He did not accept this. The water bottles are in, upper floors first. H

units.title: Laundry room: machine 2
units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: psa machine 2 in the laundry room eats 50p coins and gives nothing back. i have fed it three. it is now a very expensive piggy bank. machine 1 works but walks across the floor on spin like it's trying to leave. hold it down or it'll get to the door

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: I am glad to hear the man in 4A is recovering. I left a note, as advised. It was polite. It said the bays are marked and the markings are white. The car is now in one bay. I consider this a victory for neighbourliness and for paint.

units.title: Night knocks, Brackwater Woods (raw files)
units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Last night, west side of the reservoir, about 600 m along the path from the dam gate. Two omnis on a stand, a metre apart, gain -12, low cut at 80 Hz; the dish on the second recorder pointed north into the trees. At 03:40 there are knocks: three, a pause of about four seconds, then two. Dry, hard, wood on wood, and they carry. Minus one degree, no wind at all. Raw files attached, both recorders, untouched. Not woodpeckers, wrong hour. Not deer, nothing moved on the dish. I have no theory, just the files. Make of it what you will.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so I've just listened on proper headphones and wow, that's clean. the second set of two is slightly closer, or louder anyway, I'll do a spectrogram tomorrow with arrows. they've got a really sharp attack, like a branch on a trunk but more deliberate? not saying anything by deliberate. I just mean regular. also I know that path, the old pumping house is about 300 m north of where you'd have been

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Regular is the right word, tern. The gap inside the first three is about 0.6 seconds each, near enough. I did walk up towards the sound after the second set, maybe fifty metres, with the torch off so as not to ruin my eyes. Nothing. No movement, no further knocks for the next ninety minutes of recording. A tawny owl, a car on the dam road at 04:20. That's all.

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: headphones on for this one, and yes, with the two omnis spaced like that you can hear direction a little: the first three slightly left of centre, the two after a touch further right. Could be the same source moving, could be two sources, could be my brain making a story. Lovely clean recording either way, the frost really helps the top end.

units.author: hobby_tapeloop
units.text: Dear tern, how pleasant to see rain on a bike shed considered worth recording. In my day we did that to test the machines. I am currently working through a box of reels from my old repair shop, customers' tapes never collected, mostly weddings and budgerigars. One day I shall get through the lot and catalogue them properly. Regards, Ned

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: On the bike shed bands: if the roof panels are corrugated, you'll get resonances related to panel size and rib spacing, not neatly even, which matches what you see. Quick analysis if you post the file: I'd expect peaks somewhere between 300 Hz and 1.2 kHz. Rain is a great test signal. Better than budgerigars, sorry Ned.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: hollis you're right, peaks at 410, 780 and 1150 roughly, I'll post the screenshot with arrows. and Ned I would honestly love to hear the budgerigars. do the weddings have speeches? sorry if that's weird. also I haven't been out in the woods all week, dunlin's having all the fun

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Sieve and hose built. Wife asked where the sieve went. Tested on the breakwater in a force three: wind noise down a good 10 dB, as Hollis said, mostly in the low end. Now I can hear the pump on the fuel berth properly, which is not what I wanted, but it's honest.

units.author: lh_callcentre_tamsin
units.text: update from the helpline: the meter caller rang back. not to complain. to say goodnight. I said goodnight. my supervisor says that is not a resolution code. I have logged it as 'customer satisfied'. it's the most accurate thing I've logged all month

units.author: lh_kennel_orrin
units.text: Orrin Flats, night attendant at a boarding kennel and vet hospital. Hot chocolate from a packet. Tonight we have fourteen dogs and two very offended cats. Biscuit the beagle has worked out how to open his water bowl lid and is very pleased with himself. Juno the shepherd just wants her ears rubbed and to know where everyone is at all times.

units.author: lh_trucker_orrin
units.text: Orrin Flats, long haul, westbound with a trailer of grain dryers nobody seems to be in a hurry for. Coffee from the stop at milepost 212, which is the best coffee on this road and I'll fight you. Nothing out here but the white line and the odd set of eyes in the ditch. Mostly deer. Mostly.

units.author: lh_convenience_kestrel
units.text: Kestrel Isles, 24-hour shop, nights. Canned coffee from my own fridge, which I pay for, because I am honest and the camera is watching. Customer tonight bought one egg. Just the one. Paid with a large note. I gave him his change and he said 'that's the dream'. I don't know what he meant.

units.author: lh_student_kestrel
units.text: Kestrel Isles, campus lab, postgrad, chapter three of a thesis that I'm told is 'nearly there' by a supervisor who has never seen chapter three. Drinking: energy drink number two of a planned three. The building is empty apart from me, a fridge full of samples and a cleaner who hums. Hi everyone.

units.title: Van idling at the edge of the car park lights
units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Quiet one, but it's bugging me. A white panel van has been idling at the far edge of the car park lights since 22:50, right where the last lamp's pool stops. Engine running, headlights off. I walked past at 23:30 and 01:00: windows misted, couldn't see in. Control says leave it, probably a driver kipping with the heater on. It's 02:20. Three and a half hours of diesel.

edit.text: Quiet one, but it's bugging me. A white panel van idled at the far edge of the car park lights from 22:50, right where the last lamp's pool stops. Engine running, headlights off. I walked past at 23:30 and 01:00: windows misted, couldn't see in. Control said leave it. Edit: it's gone. It pulled out at 02:45 with its lights still off, so closer to four hours. I was at the barrier end and didn't see anyone get in or out.

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Procedure where I work: log time in, time out, plate, position. Note whether exhaust is visible. Do not approach a running vehicle alone. If Control says leave it, log that Control said leave it, with the time. Then it's his van, not yours.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: The boring and serious answer: people do sleep in vans with the engine on for the heater, and every winter a few of them don't wake up, because exhaust gets into the cab. If you see one again, a knock on the window is a kindness, not an intrusion. Misted windows usually mean someone's breathing inside.

units.author: lh_taxi_halvard
units.text:
every cabbie in Halvard has slept in his car with the engine running at the hospital rank
not proud of it
the trick is you crack a window
anyway four hours is a long kip but I've done five on a bad week

units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Housekeeping: thanks for not posting the plate, Dev. Please keep it that way, everyone, for vans, cars and neighbours. Dmitra's point is the important one. If something looks wrong with a person, it's a phone call to the right people, not a thread.

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Fair point Dmitra, and you're right that the windows were misted, I hadn't thought of it like that. Next time I'll knock. Control said the same thing in a less nice way. Still odd that it went off with no lights. Anyway. Logged it, as gate7 says, with the time Control said leave it.

units.title: 3am callers (anonymised, with love)
units.author: lh_callcentre_tamsin
units.text: Starting a thread for helpline nights. Caller one: wanted us to switch off 'just the street lamp outside' because it shines into her bedroom. That's the council, madam, but I admire the ambition. Caller two: a man who reads his meter to me every night 'for practice'. Caller three: dead air for forty seconds, then a cough, then they hung up. That's the shift so far.

units.author: lh_kennel_orrin
units.text: The meter-reading man is my favourite person this week and I've never met him. Practice for what? The meter exam? I hope you never find out. Some mysteries should be left to grow.

units.author: lh_trucker_orrin
units.text: Dead air with a cough is a trucker's pocket dial nine times out of ten, darlin'. Phone in the shirt pocket, seat belt presses the screen. I've rung my ex-wife four times that way. She's never once believed it.

units.author: lh_callcentre_tamsin
units.text: merle that would explain an alarming number of my calls. caller four tonight: a woman asking whether a power cut 'counts' if it only happens in her kitchen. it does not count. it's a fuse. I talked her through it. her kitchen came back and she cheered. best part of the job, honestly

units.title: Microsleeps on the drive home: how do you handle them?
units.author: lh_trucker_orrin
units.text: Long-haul advice nobody asked for. Highway hypnosis is real: forty miles of the same white line and your brain starts filing the road under 'already seen'. Signs it's got you: you can't remember the last town, or you see things on the shoulder that turn into mailboxes. Fix: pull over, twenty-minute nap, coffee before the nap not after, stretch your legs round the rig. Never 'push through'. The road doesn't care how tough you are.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: This is good advice, and the coffee-then-nap order is right: caffeine takes about twenty minutes to land, so you wake up just as it arrives. The bit about seeing things on the shoulder is worth underlining. A tired brain fills in the edges of your vision with whatever it expects. It isn't a failing. It's a brain doing its best with too little.

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: My drive home is only twenty minutes, past the Brackwater junction, and it still gets me some mornings. Those temporary lights are the only thing keeping me awake. I sit at the red and count the cones. Never thought I'd be grateful to roadworks.

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: I get the staff bus from the depot home love so I'm all right but the drivers who do the first runs say exactly the same, they all do the window down and a sweet in the cheek trick, one of them sings hymns to himself, the passengers don't mind, I think they find it nice

units.title: Vending machine tier list (hospital edition)
units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: Port Ammet General vending tier list, from a man who has used all of them on a trolley run. Top: machine 3, ground floor (the double cup, see previous). Good: the one by Maternity, best crisps. Fine: Outpatients, if it's working, which it isn't. Bottom: the one on B corridor that takes your money and hums at you. Nobody uses it. It hums anyway.

units.author: lh_picker_weyhaven
units.text: warehouse tier: there is one machine. it sells one kind of sandwich, egg, and it's always out of egg. we've started calling it the shrine. you go and stand in front of it at break and think about what could have been

units.author: lh_nurse_halvard
units.text: Our ward has a toaster. Officially it doesn't exist. Every night at 3 the whole corridor smells of toast and nobody admits to anything. Better than any machine. Back to it.

units.title: Thesis survival list, night edition
units.author: lh_student_kestrel
units.text: Things that are keeping me alive at 3am: 1. the lab's good chair, which I hide behind the fume cupboard before I leave; 2. a playlist called 'do not cry'; 3. the cleaner who hums; 4. the vending machine on floor 2 that gives free noodles if you press B4 twice. Things that are not: 1. chapter three. That's the list.

units.author: lh_convenience_kestrel
units.text: Students come in at 4am and buy the same three things: noodles, an energy drink, a single banana. The banana is a cry for help. You are doing the banana stage. You'll be fine.

units.title: Gilliver slip lights
units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: Gilliver slip last night: two lights out of six, same as before. Bottom of the slip in pitch dark with the weed on it. I had the good torch, Finn didn't, and he nearly went in on the wet bit at the bottom with a rope in his hand. Someone needs to fix those before the fog comes in, because in fog you'll see nothing at all.

units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Thank you, Kerris, and I'm sorry. The coastguard notice went out this morning. The electrician is booked, but the fittings on the lower slip are an old pattern and two need ordering. Until then I'll put two battery lamps at the bottom of the slip at dusk myself. Under byelaw 9 the bottom of the slip is closed to the public after dark anyway.

units.author: deckhand_finn
units.text: for the record I did not 'nearly go in', I did a very controlled slide with a rope in my hand and stopped exactly where I meant to, which was nearly in. thanks Quill. battery lamps would be class. also whoever keeps fishing off the bottom of the slip at night, it's not you that's getting hit with the bow line

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: Quill I've got two big battery lamps in the back of the chandlery you can have. on the house. dont let anyone nick them, they're the good ones

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: Logged both nights in the deck log and sent the harbour office a copy. In the meantime, crew will put the forward flood on the slip as we come alongside at Gilliver, and nobody goes down the bottom section without a torch. Kerris, thanks for the good torch.

units.title: lisle pier evening report
units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: Lisle pier, evening shift... all pier lights working, which, ha, after the power went this morning I wasn't sure. The transformer man came and went. 17:50 boat in on time, two cars, a man with a bicycle and a goat in a crate. The goat was very calm. Calmer than me, anyway.

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: The goat's called Margaret and she's on the vehicle deck once a month going to the vet. She's the best-behaved passenger we carry. Ada, if your lights are working, can you send some over to Gilliver?

units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: ha, I'd post them over if I could... Margaret is lovely. She looked at me the whole time I was doing the ropes, like she was checking my knots. Anyway the late one's due, back to it.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Prices today. Cod up to 4.30, haddock steady, crab still poor. Calm as a millpond out there, sea like oil off the Holm side. Water's flushing on Quay Row, so the tea in the chandlery tasted of iron, Rook, I'm sorry to say. Glass high and steady. Fog's coming. I can smell it.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: the tea always tastes of iron bram, that's the kettle not the water main. fog lamps and horns in stock lads, before you all come in at once on friday wanting them

units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: For anyone wondering, the contractor's boat movements are on the harbour office board each morning, next to the tide times. It's usually one run out at the top of the tide and back within two hours. Please don't hail the skipper for gossip about the island. He has a schedule and a lot of fuel drums.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Never hailed a man for gossip in my life, Quill. I only waved. He waved back and shouted 'cold out there'. That's all the gossip there is. Cold out there.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Book written up properly, stay wire first as told. Today was the Lisle transformer fuse, which went pop at 08:12 and took the school dinners with it. And we started the Brackwater substation inspection: thermal camera on every joint, nothing hotter than it should be. Garvey says it's the most boring substation in the Sound. He says it fondly.

units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: Boring's the best thing a substation can be. That one went in with the dam in the sixties and it's had a quiet life. Bushings are getting on, mind. I've told them twice. Write that in your book too, Tess, so when one goes there's a page with a date on it that says somebody said.
